feed.title: Regulation · United States · Diting Lab
feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: CFTC Wins Court Order Requiring Two Defendants to Pay Over $31 Million in Digital Asset and Precious Metals Fraud
entry.summary: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and Arkansas Woman to Pay Over $31 Million for Digital Assets, Precious Metals Fraud CFTC · Sep 30, 2026 · Crypto The CFTC announced that a federal court in the Middle District of Florida entered a default judgment against Brian Early and Alisha Ann Kingrey for their roles in a digital asset and precious metals fraud involving Fundsz. The court ordered $15,732,455 in restitution and a $15,752,455 civil penalty, permanently enjoined further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations, and imposed permanent registration and trading bans. Separately, consent orders against Rene Larralde's estate representative and Juan Pablo Valcarce required over $2.7 million in assets to be turned over to a court-appointed receiver.

entry.title: CFTC Wins Court Orders Totaling Over $288 Million Against Former Long Island Resident and Firm in Commodity Pool Ponzi Case
entry.summary: CFTC Secures Federal Court Orders Requiring Former Long Island Resident and His Firm to Pay Over $288 Million for Operating a Commodity Pool Ponzi Scheme CFTC · Oct 19, 2026 · Crypto The CFTC announced that a federal court in the Southern District of New York entered orders against Eddy Alexandre and his company EminiFX Inc., requiring $228,576,962 in restitution, $15,049,500 in disgorgement, and a $45,148,500 civil monetary penalty. The court found EminiFX was a Ponzi scheme that induced investors with misrepresentations about cryptocurrency and Forex trading. Alexandre is also serving a nine-year prison sentence in a parallel criminal case.

entry.title: SEC Charges Entities in Fraud Schemes Totaling at Least $15 Million Lured Investors via WhatsApp
entry.summary: SEC Charges Multiple Entities in Fraud Schemes Totaling at Least $15 Million That Used WhatsApp and Other Platforms to Lure Investors SEC · Sep 29, 2026 · Crypto Not enough source text for a summary

entry.title: SEC proposal on how advisers and regulated funds may custody crypto assets
entry.summary: SEC Proposal Would Address How Investment Advisers and Funds Can Custody Crypto Assets Under the Federal Securities Laws SEC · Oct 2, 2026 · Crypto The SEC proposed new rules and amendments creating a framework for registered investment advisers and regulated funds to custody crypto assets. The proposal would allow self-custody of crypto assets under certain conditions and permit state trust companies to act as custodians. The public comment period is 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

entry.title: Federal Register: Proposed Agency Information Collection Activities, Comment Request (October 9, 2026)
entry.summary: Proposed Agency Information Collection Activities; Comment Request Federal Register · Oct 9, 2026 · Crypto The National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) published a notice requesting public comment on proposed revisions to the NCUA Form 5300 Call Report, with comments due by December 8, 2026. The revision adds a new Schedule J, Payment Stablecoin Activities, to collect data on reserve asset custody, cryptographic key custody and control, direct exposure to permitted payment stablecoin issuers, and payment stablecoins held on the balance sheet. The proposed changes would take effect with the March 31, 2027 report date.

entry.title: Cboe EDGX Exchange proposes rule changes setting listing standards for options on crypto-holding commodity trusts
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 19.3 and Rule 19.4 To Establish Generic Listing Criteria and Continued Listing Standards for Options on Commodity-Based Trusts Holding Multiple Crypto Assets and To Permit the Listing of Options on Exchange-Traded Funds Federal Register · Oct 22, 2026 · Crypto Cboe EDGX Exchange filed a proposal with the SEC to amend Rules 19.3 and 19.4. It would set generic listing and continued listing standards for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets, and permit options on exchange-traded funds. The proposal mirrors rules already approved for Cboe Options, was filed as non-controversial, took immediate effect, and invites public comment.

entry.title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations web general licenses 46C, 47A, 48B, 50B, 51B, 52A, and 54A
entry.summary: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 46C, 47A, 48B, 50B, 51B, 52A, and 54A Federal Register · Sep 30, 2026 The Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control publishes seven general licenses issued under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations, previously posted on its website. Each license replaces an earlier version. The notice reproduces the license texts, which authorize specified transactions otherwise prohibited by the regulations.

entry.title: Treasury publishes eight Venezuela Sanctions Regulations general licenses, including GL 46D on Venezuelan oil
entry.summary: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 46D, 47B, 48C, 50C, 51C, 52B, 54B, and 61A Federal Register · Sep 30, 2026 The Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control published in the Federal Register eight general licenses issued under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations: GLs 46D, 47B, 48C, 50C, 51C, 52B, 54B and 61A, which had previously been posted on OFAC's website. The document sets out the text of each license. GL 46D authorizes certain transactions involving Venezuelan-origin oil or petrochemical products, subject to conditions on payments and reporting.

entry.title: Proposed rules on custody of crypto assets by advisers and regulated funds
entry.summary: Adviser and Regulated Fund Custody Rules; Crypto Custody Rules Federal Register · Oct 6, 2026 · Crypto The SEC proposes new custody rules under the Investment Company Act addressing how regulated investment companies may custody crypto securities and similar investments. It also proposes amendments to the Advisers Act custody rule covering how registered investment advisers may custody client crypto funds and securities. The proposal includes related reporting and recordkeeping changes and amendments to Forms ADV and N-CEN.

entry.title: Treasury Notice Appointing Senior Executive Service Performance Review Board Members
entry.summary: Senior Executive Service Performance Review Boards Federal Register · Oct 16, 2026 The U.S. Treasury Department published a Federal Register notice announcing appointments to its Senior Executive Service Performance Review Boards (PRBs). The boards review and make recommendations on performance appraisals, ratings, bonuses and other personnel actions for senior executive positions. The notice lists officials from across Treasury, including offices such as the Office of Foreign Assets Control and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.

entry.title: CFTC to hold roundtable on 24/7 trading
entry.summary: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading CFTC · Oct 28, 2026 The Commodity Futures Trading Commission will host an industry roundtable on December 15 to discuss whether derivatives markets can move to 24/7 trading. It builds on the CFTC's Request for Comment on the topic issued earlier this summer. Topics include overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure, staffing, and operational readiness. The event is open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov.

entry.title: NCUA Draft 2027–2028 Budget for Public Comment
entry.summary: NCUA Draft 2027-2028 Budget Federal Register · Oct 28, 2026 The National Credit Union Administration published its draft 2027–2028 budget for public review as required by federal statute. The draft covers the Operating Budget, Capital Budget, and Share Insurance Fund Administrative Budget, with personnel and dollar estimates for each. A public budget hearing is scheduled for November 17, 2026, and written comments are due by November 30, 2026.

entry.title: CFTC-Kansas State Agricultural Futures Conference (AgCon 2026) recap
entry.summary: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 CFTC · Oct 27, 2026 The CFTC and Kansas State University's Risk Management Center co-hosted the two-day 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference in Overland Park, Kansas. Sessions covered challenges facing the farm economy, derivatives market developments and risk management tools for producers. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig gave remarks and took part in several discussions.

entry.title: CFTC Sues Utah to Block State Enforcement Against Regulated Markets
entry.summary: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction CFTC · Oct 27, 2026 The CFTC has sued Utah to stop the state from using state laws to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets. Utah had filed civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said Congress made the CFTC the sole federal regulator of these event contract markets and the agency will defend that authority.

entry.title: CFTC announces twice-weekly publication of the Commitments of Traders (COT) Report
entry.summary: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report CFTC · Oct 27, 2026 CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced plans to increase the COT Report's publication frequency from once to twice weekly by the end of 2026. Monday data will be published Wednesday and Wednesday data Friday, both at 3:30 p.m. ET, cutting reporting latency from three days to two.

entry.title: Order granting temporary registration of Cboe Clear U.S. as a clearing agency under the Exchange Act
entry.summary: Cboe Clear U.S., LLC; Order Granting an Application, as Amended, for Temporary Registration as a Clearing Agency Under Section 17A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 Federal Register · Oct 27, 2026 The SEC grants Cboe Clear U.S., LLC (CCUS) temporary registration as a clearing agency to provide central counterparty services for binary options that are securities. The order also exempts CCUS from certain requirements for 18 months from its date. Reasons are set out in Parts III and IV of the order.)

entry.title: Notice of regulatory waivers approved for Q1 2026 by HUD
entry.summary: Notice of Regulatory Waiver Requests Granted for the First Quarter of Calendar Year 2026 Federal Register · Oct 27, 2026 The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development publishes this quarterly notice under section 106 of the HUD Reform Act, listing regulatory waivers it approved from January 1 to March 31, 2026. The waivers are grouped by HUD program office and list the project, the waived provision, the approving official, and the grounds for approval. Contact details are provided for obtaining more information on specific waivers.

entry.title: Notice establishing the Advisory Council on Health and Human Performance Optimization under the Department of Defense
entry.summary: Establishment of Federal Advisory Committees-Advisory Council on Health and Human Performance Optimization Federal Register · Oct 27, 2026 The Department of Defense (Department of War) announces the establishment of the Advisory Council on Health and Human Performance Optimization as a discretionary federal advisory committee. The Council will provide independent advice on optimizing warfighter health and performance. Members serve without compensation and receive only travel and per diem reimbursement.

entry.title: CFTC Obtains Court Order Requiring Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud Case
entry.summary: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Louisiana Man and His Companies to Pay Over $9 Million in Forex Fraud CFTC · Oct 21, 2026 The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced that a federal court in Louisiana entered a default judgment against Michael B. DePetrillo and two of his companies over a fraudulent retail forex scheme. The court found they misappropriated more than $3 million from participants through false statements and Ponzi-like payments. The defendants were ordered to pay a $9,211,492 civil monetary penalty, permanently enjoined from further Commodity Exchange Act violations, and banned from trading and registration.

entry.title: CFTC and NBA sign agreement to protect professional basketball integrity in prediction markets
entry.summary: CFTC and National Basketball Association Sign MOU to Protect Integrity in Professional Basketball CFTC · Oct 26, 2026 The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the National Basketball Association signed a Memorandum of Understanding to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets. Under the MOU, the two organizations will regularly communicate about integrity matters and share information to help keep prediction markets fair and transparent. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said the agreement continues the Commission's push for greater data sharing with professional sports leagues.

entry.title: Treasury and IRS propose rules for paying tax on certain farmland sales in installments
entry.summary: Treasury, IRS issue proposed regulations on installment payments for tax on certain farmland sales IRS · Sep 28, 2026 The Treasury and IRS issued proposed regulations for taxpayers who sell or exchange qualifying farmland to qualified farmers and elect to pay the resulting tax in four equal annual installments. Under Section 1062 of the Internal Revenue Code, the election applies to qualified sales made in taxable years beginning after July 4, 2025. The proposal also covers sales by partnerships, S corporations, trusts and estates, and explains how the 10-year farming-use requirement can be met. Comments are due by November 30, 2026."},

entry.title: IRS extends relief to taxpayers affected by Israel events, postponing eligible filing and payment deadlines to Sept. 30, 2027
entry.summary: IRS announces new relief for eligible taxpayers affected by ongoing events in Israel: due dates for eligible returns and payments may be postponed to Sept. 30, 2027; additional relief may be available IRS · Sep 30, 2026 The IRS announced additional tax relief for individuals and businesses affected by the ongoing conflict in Israel, postponing a wide range of federal filing, payment and other time-sensitive tax deadlines until Sept. 30, 2027. Notice 2026-63 follows earlier notices 2023-71, 2024-72 and 2025-53, covering taxpayers in Israel, the West Bank and Gaza.

entry.title: IRS recruits volunteers and community partners for free tax preparation help
entry.summary: The IRS seeks community partners and volunteers to support free tax services IRS · Oct 1, 2026 The IRS is seeking volunteers and community partners for its VITA and TCE programs, which offer free tax preparation during the upcoming filing season. No experience is required, and the IRS provides free training. Interested individuals can sign up through an online form and will receive a list of local sites and a virtual orientation invitation.

entry.title: Treasury and IRS propose rules for Education Freedom Tax Credit
entry.summary: The Trump administration advances the establishment of America’s first nationwide school choice program IRS · Oct 1, 2026 The Treasury and IRS issued proposed regulations implementing the Education Freedom Tax Credit under section 25F. The credit lets individuals claim up to $1,700 for qualified cash contributions to Scholarship Granting Organizations, or up to $3,400 for joint filers, to fund K-12 scholarships. It takes effect January 1, 2027.](Summary)

entry.title: IRS reminder on simple steps to protect tax data during Cybersecurity Awareness Month
entry.summary: IRS reminder: Cybersecurity Awareness Month offers simple steps to protect tax data IRS · Oct 2, 2026 The IRS urges taxpayers, tax professionals and organizations to adopt basic online security habits during Cybersecurity Awareness Month. Recommended steps include using strong unique passwords, turning on multifactor authentication, installing updates, recognizing and reporting scams, and avoiding public Wi-Fi. The notice also describes IRS secure tools such as the Identity Protection PIN and online tax accounts, and how to identify and report IRS impersonation scams.

entry.title: IRS highlights cooperation with UK tax authority's new whistleblower program
entry.summary: IRS highlights partnership with UK tax authority’s new whistleblower program IRS · Oct 7, 2026 The IRS said the UK's HMRC whistleblower program, the Strengthened Reward Scheme launched in November 2025, drew on the IRS Whistleblower Office's expertise. The program encourages reports of serious tax avoidance and evasion by wealthy individuals and large businesses. The two agencies say the collaboration aims to deter cross-border tax evasion, and the release lists examples such as undeclared foreign bank accounts and money laundering.

entry.title: IRS Offers Excise Tax Relief for Dyed Diesel Fuel Following Executive Order
entry.summary: IRS provides dyed diesel fuel relief related to excise tax following President Trump’s Executive Order IRS · Oct 14, 2026 The IRS will not impose penalties on dyed diesel fuel sold for or used on highways nationwide, in response to an October 5, 2026 Executive Order. The relief is retroactive to October 1, 2026, and runs through December 31, 2026. It applies only to federal tax purposes and does not affect state fuel taxes or penalties.

entry.title: Treasury and IRS propose rules to protect health benefits for eligible Americans
entry.summary: Treasury and IRS move to protect health care benefits for eligible Americans IRS · Oct 14, 2026 The Treasury and IRS issued proposed regulations implementing reforms to the Premium Tax Credit, a refundable credit that helps taxpayers buy health insurance through the Health Insurance Exchanges. The rules aim to prevent fraud and abuse. Beginning in 2027, eligibility would be restricted to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and certain lawfully present noncitizens, with new verification criteria for advance payments.

entry.title: IRS announces 2026 Tax Professional Awareness Week with resources for the 2027 filing season
entry.summary: IRS announces 2026 Tax Professional Awareness Week, highlighting resources to help tax professionals prepare for the 2027 filing season IRS · Oct 16, 2026 The IRS announced Tax Professional Awareness Week, held the week of October 19, to help tax professionals prepare for the 2027 filing season. The week features webinars, instructional videos, tax tips and tools on accurate return preparation, due diligence, identity theft prevention and cybersecurity. An October 21 webinar on refundable credits is scheduled.

entry.title: IRS begins automatic refunds for adoption tax credit carryforwards from prior years
entry.summary: IRS has begun issuing automatic refunds to individuals who claimed Adoption Tax Credit carryforward from prior years IRS · Oct 16, 2026 The IRS has begun issuing refunds to more than 50,000 taxpayers who used adoption tax credit carryforwards and expects most to be completed by year-end. Treasury clarified that, for tax year 2025 only, carryforwards from 2020 to 2024 can increase the refundable adoption credit, subject to a $5,000 per qualifying child limit. Affected taxpayers do not need to file amended returns, and the IRS will notify them of adjustments.

entry.title: Temporary Reporting and Recordkeeping Relief for Certain Dyed Diesel Fuel Taxes
entry.summary: Temporary reporting and recordkeeping relief for certain fuel uses IRS · Oct 21, 2026 The IRS announced temporary administrative relief from reporting and recordkeeping requirements for liability under section 4041(a) arising from taxable uses of dyed diesel between Oct. 1, 2026, and Jan. 1, 2027. The IRS will not assert civil penalties or additions to tax for covered failures, including filing Form 720 solely to report that liability. No subsequent filing or record reconstruction is required after Dec. 31, 2026, and obligations for other liabilities remain unchanged.

entry.title: IRS reminder to protect tax information now, including online credentials and IP PINs
entry.summary: IRS reminder: Take steps now to protect tax information IRS · Oct 22, 2026 The IRS reminded taxpayers to guard against tax-related identity theft by safeguarding their online account sign-in credentials and obtaining an Identity Protection PIN (IP PIN). The six-digit IP PIN prevents others from filing federal returns using a taxpayer's Social Security number or ITIN. Taxpayers planning to file early in 2027 should request an IP PIN before the online system goes offline for annual maintenance in mid-November, and it is generally available again from mid-January.

entry.title: Treasury and IRS update retirement plan correction program and create one for IRAs
entry.summary: Treasury, IRS update retirement plan correction program and establish correction program for individual retirement accounts IRS · Oct 22, 2026 The Treasury and IRS issued two revenue procedures. Revenue Procedure 2026-34 updates the Employee Plans Compliance Resolution System and took effect the day it was issued. Revenue Procedure 2026-33 creates the IRA Compliance Resolution System, which lets IRA custodians and owners request correction of certain errors caused by service providers and request waivers of the 60-day rollover requirement, effective May 1, 2027.

entry.title: IRS reminder to plan taxes year-round to make filing easier
entry.summary: IRS reminder: Year-round tax planning can make filing easier IRS · Oct 23, 2026 The IRS encourages taxpayers to take simple steps now, such as checking withholding, organizing records, using IRS online tools, and protecting personal information, to prepare for the 2027 filing season. The attached Publication 5349-A, Year-Round Tax Planning is for Everyone, offers practical tips and IRS resources. It also warns taxpayers about scams and advises them not to click unexpected links.

entry.title: CFTC Staff Extends Brexit-Related No-Action Relief
entry.summary: CFTC Staff Extends Brexit-Related No-Action Positions CFTC · Oct 1, 2026 The CFTC's Market Participants Division and Division of Market Oversight extended temporary no-action positions tied to the UK's withdrawal from the EU. The positions aim to maintain regulatory certainty for derivatives trading and clearing between the UK and the US. Staff said keeping them in place remains appropriate while the CFTC works with UK authorities on UK law and possible comparability determinations.

entry.title: CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Proposed Rules for Crypto Asset Transactions and Crypto Asset Markets
entry.summary: CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Relating to Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets CFTC · Oct 6, 2026 · Crypto The CFTC has published an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeking public comment on a planned comprehensive framework for retail commodity transactions involving crypto assets under section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act. The notice asks how the Commission can prevent abusive practices, provide crypto-specific guidance on industry best practices, and codify a designated contract market subcategory called a crypto asset market. Comments are due within 60 days of Federal Register publication.

entry.title: CFTC no-action letter lets exchanges convert perpetual-style index futures into true perpetual futures.
entry.summary: CFTC Issues No-Action Letter for DCMs Regarding Converting Existing Perpetual-Style Broad-Based Security Index Futures into True Perpetual Futures CFTC · Oct 6, 2026 The CFTC's Division of Market Oversight has issued no-action relief allowing designated contract markets to convert existing perpetual-style broad-based security index futures into true perpetual futures. DCMs may remove expiration dates once they meet conditions in the letter, including soliciting market participant feedback, giving advance notice and an exit opportunity, providing risk disclosures, and not changing other material terms. DCMs must file amendments under CFTC Regulations 40.5 or 40.6 and certify compliance. The no-action positions expire on October 20, 2026.

entry.title: CFTC Issues Rule Excluding Certain Gambling Activity from the Swap Definition
entry.summary: CFTC Issues Interim Final Rule Excluding Certain Activity from the Definition of Swap CFTC · Oct 10, 2026 The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an interim final rule confirming that casino-style gambling products, including sportsbook and casino game wagers, are excluded from the definition of “swap.” The rule takes effect upon publication in the Federal Register, and written comments are due within 30 days via Regulations.gov.

entry.title: CFTC Seeks Comment on Proposal to Include Certain Event Contracts in the Swap Definition
entry.summary: CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Concerning the Inclusion of Certain Event Contracts in the Definition of Swap CFTC · Oct 10, 2026 The Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a proposed rule that would expressly define "swap" to include event contracts based on sports, politics, cultural, and weather-related events. The proposal states these contracts are commonly known in the trade as swaps and aims to resolve any ambiguity about them. Comments must be submitted via Regulations.gov within 30 days of Federal Register publication.

entry.title: CFTC Innovation Task Force Releases Agenda for First Super Intelligence Frontier Forum
entry.summary: CFTC’s Innovation Task Force Announces Agenda & Panelists for Inaugural Frontier Forum on Super Intelligence CFTC · Oct 21, 2026 The CFTC's Innovation Task Force released the agenda for its inaugural Frontier Forum on Super Intelligence. Discussions will cover how super intelligence is being implemented at the frontier, its impact on U.S. markets, and the Commission's role in fostering responsible adoption while protecting market participants from emerging risks. The meeting will be streamed live on CFTC.gov.

entry.title: SEC charges investment adviser Zoe Financial with failing to disclose conflicts of interest
entry.summary: SEC Charges Registered Investment Adviser Zoe Financial for Failure to Disclose Conflict of Interest SEC · Sep 29, 2026 The SEC announced settled charges against New York investment adviser Zoe Financial Inc. for failing to fully disclose conflicts of interest to clients. The firm's referral network encouraged advisers to use its Zoe Wealth platform, and salespeople often recommended advisers beyond the algorithm's matches. The company agreed to a cease-and-desist order, censure, and a $450,000 civil penalty without admitting the findings.

entry.title: SEC proposes rule changes to widen retail access to private markets
entry.summary: SEC Proposes Amendments to Expand Responsible Retailization of Private Markets SEC · Oct 1, 2026 The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission proposed amendments to expand retail investor choice and promote innovation in regulated fund structures while keeping investor protections. The proposals would let registered investment advisers receive performance-based compensation based on capital gains from clients including regulated funds, modernize the interval fund framework, and create a rules-based framework for closed-end funds to issue multiple share classes. The Commission also seeks comment on adding a FINRA-developed accredited investor exam and certain professional credentials as ways to qualify as accredited investors.

entry.title: SEC charges two men over fraud scheme targeting veterans
entry.summary: SEC Charges Two Individuals With Orchestrating Fraud Scheme That Targeted Veterans SEC · Oct 1, 2026 The SEC charged Christopher Kenji Dinelli and Jacob David Frankel with orchestrating a fraud that raised over $8.7 million from 35 investors through a fund and an advisory firm. The complaint alleges they made false claims about past returns and client base, and diverted investor money to losing trades and personal expenses. The civil case was filed in federal court in Manhattan, alongside parallel criminal charges.

entry.title: SEC sues Meyer Global Management and its CEO for defrauding retail investors in private funds holding SpaceX and other pre-IPO securities.
entry.summary: SEC Charges Meyer Global Management and Its CEO With Defrauding Retail Investors in Private Funds That Held Interests in SpaceX and Other Pre-IPO Securities SEC · Oct 1, 2026 The SEC has charged private fund adviser Meyer Global Management LLC and its CEO, Owen E.H. Meyer, with defrauding investors in funds holding SpaceX and other pre-IPO securities. The complaint alleges misuse of client fund assets for Meyer's personal expenses, concealment of these actions, and a failure to meet a capital call that led to the loss of a nearly $3,000,000 SpaceX investment. The case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, with the SEC seeking permanent injunctions, disgorgement, and civil penalties.

entry.title: SEC publishes new handbook explaining its examination process
entry.summary: SEC’s Division of Examinations Announces New Exam Handbook SEC · Oct 2, 2026 The SEC's Division of Examinations published a new handbook, "The SEC Exam Handbook: A Practical Guide on Process and Engagement," replacing the earlier examination brochure. It explains each stage of an exam, from risk assessment through the disposition letter, and lists ways for registrants to give feedback. The document states that exams aim to improve compliance, monitor risk, and prevent fraud.

entry.title: SEC and Global Regulators Issue Joint Investor Bulletin on Fraud Awareness During World Investor Week
entry.summary: SEC Coordinates with Global Financial Regulators to Raise Fraud Awareness During World Investor Week SEC · Oct 5, 2026 The SEC, with other U.S. and global financial regulators, issued a joint investor bulletin as part of World Investor Week. It urges investors to stay resilient amid changing economic conditions and to watch for rising relationship investment and impersonation scams. The SEC also points investors to free education resources on Investor.gov.

entry.title: SEC Announces Virtual Compliance Seminar for Investment Companies and Advisers
entry.summary: SEC to Host Virtual National Compliance Outreach Seminar for Investment Companies and Investment Advisers SEC · Oct 6, 2026 The SEC's Compliance Outreach Program will host a virtual national seminar on November 19, 2026, for investment companies and investment advisers. The event aims to help chief compliance officers strengthen compliance programs to protect investors. Panels cover information security, operational resiliency, registered and private fund adviser topics, and compliance program effectiveness. Advance registration is not required, and the live webcast link will be posted on SEC.gov that morning.

entry.title: SEC seeks final judgment against former Western Asset co-CIO Ken Leech in cherry-picking case
entry.summary: SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Former Western Asset Co-CIO Ken Leech in Cherry Picking Case SEC · Oct 7, 2026 The SEC has asked a court to approve a consent final judgment against Stephen Kenneth Leech II, former co-chief investment officer of Western Asset Management, over an alleged scheme of allocating favorable trades to certain portfolios and unfavorable trades to others. The proposed judgment would require a $3 million penalty, an officer-and-director bar, and a permanent injunction against antifraud violations. Western Asset separately agreed in June 2026 to a $100 million civil penalty and a Fair Fund for affected investors.

entry.title: SEC Proposes Wider Securities Eligible for Fund Cross Trades
entry.summary: SEC Proposes Expanding Securities Eligible for Cross Trading by Registered Funds SEC · Oct 9, 2026 The SEC proposed amendments to Rule 17a-7 under the Investment Company Act, which allows registered funds to trade securities with certain affiliates under set conditions. The changes would expand eligible securities, including most fixed-income securities, modernize pricing and oversight conditions, and add enhanced investor protections. The proposal would also require aggregated reporting of trading activity and cross trades on Forms N-PORT and N-MFP, with a 60-day comment period after Federal Register publication.

entry.title: SEC Advisory Committee to Discuss IPO Modernization and Crowdfunding Rules
entry.summary: SEC Small Business Advisory Committee to Discuss IPO Modernization and Regulation Crowdfunding SEC · Oct 14, 2026 The SEC's Small Business Capital Formation Advisory Committee will hold a public meeting on October 27, 2026, to continue discussing IPO modernization. The afternoon session will examine Regulation Crowdfunding, including its current framework, successes, challenges, and potential policy changes to expand early-stage capital raising. The meeting will be held at SEC headquarters and streamed live on SEC.gov.

entry.title: SEC Announces Roundtable on Machine-Understandable Data for Super Intelligence
entry.summary: SEC Announces Roundtable on Machine-Understandable Data in the Age of Super Intelligence SEC · Oct 20, 2026 The SEC will host a public roundtable on November 9, 2026, to discuss the use of machine-understandable data and Super Intelligence, along with related risks and costs. The event will be held at SEC headquarters and streamed live on SEC.gov, with a recording available later.

entry.title: SEC and Japan's FSA hold autumn financial regulatory dialogue
entry.summary: SEC, FSA Hold Autumn Financial Regulatory Dialogue SEC · Oct 20, 2026 The U.S. SEC and Japan's Financial Services Agency met in Tokyo on October 19, 2026, for their autumn financial regulatory dialogue, building on longstanding cooperation. Participants discussed recent market developments, both agencies' strategic priorities, and regulatory matters including private and public markets, asset management, and innovation. The next dialogue is scheduled for spring 2027 in Washington, D.C.

entry.title: SEC and French AMF sign MOU to boost cooperation on investment advisers
entry.summary: SEC and AMF Announce Supervisory MOU To Enhance Cooperation for Investment Advisers and Investment Service Providers SEC · Oct 20, 2026 The SEC and France's AMF signed a memorandum of understanding to facilitate consultation and information-sharing on supervising investment advisers, investment companies and investment service providers. The MOU facilitates SEC registration of AMF-supervised asset managers seeking to advise clients in the United States, and the SEC will process new and pending applications under this arrangement.

entry.title: SEC Announces Fiscal Year 2027 Examination Priorities
entry.summary: SEC Announces Fiscal Year 2027 Examination Priorities SEC · Oct 23, 2026 The SEC's Division of Examinations has released its priorities for fiscal year 2027, identifying areas of focus across registrants such as investment advisers, broker-dealers, and clearing agencies. Key areas include retail investor protection, private funds and private credit, cybersecurity, emerging technologies, and market infrastructure such as Treasury clearing and tokenization. The document states the list is not exhaustive and that focus areas may be adjusted in response to market developments.

entry.title: Proposed amendments on cross trades between registered funds and affiliates
entry.summary: Investment Company Cross Trading Federal Register · Oct 15, 2026 The SEC proposes amending Rule 17a-7 under the Investment Company Act, which permits cross trades between a registered fund and certain affiliates subject to conditions. The changes would expand eligible securities, modernize conditions, and strengthen investor protection. The SEC also proposes aggregated reporting of trading activity and cross trades on Forms N-PORT and N-MFP. Comments are due December 14, 2026.

entry.title: SEC notice: Cboe EDGX proposal to update the definition of "Trading Platform" in its fee schedule
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Update the Definition of Trading Platform Federal Register · Oct 26, 2026 The SEC published a proposed rule change filed by Cboe EDGX Exchange to amend the definition of "Trading Platform" in its fee schedule. The current definition covers only registered national securities exchanges, alternative trading systems, and electronic communications networks. The proposal adds a functional, use-based category for any other system or platform that systematically executes orders of persons other than its operator by electronic means. Non-exhaustive examples include broker crossing systems not filed as ATSs, systematic internalization systems, and decentralized blockchain-based or tokenized environments.

entry.title: SEC notice on Cboe BZX proposal to update the fee schedule definition of "Trading Platform"
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Update the Definition of Trading Platform Federal Register · Oct 26, 2026 Cboe BZX Exchange proposed a rule change to broaden the definition of "Trading Platform" in its fee schedule. The amendment adds a functional category covering any system through which orders of persons other than the operator are systematically executed electronically. Examples include broker crossing systems not filed as ATSs, systematic internalization systems, and decentralized or tokenized environments.

entry.title: Notice of a proposed rule change by Cboe EDGA Exchange to update the definition of “Trading Platform” in its fee schedule
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Update the Definition of Trading Platform Federal Register · Oct 26, 2026 The SEC published notice of Cboe EDGA Exchange's proposed rule change to amend the definition of “Trading Platform” in its fee schedule. The change adds a functional, use-based category covering any other system or platform that systematically executes orders of persons other than the operator by electronic means. Examples cited include broker crossing systems not filed as ATSs, systematic internalization systems, and decentralized blockchain-based or tokenized environments.

entry.title: Cboe BYX Exchange notice of proposed fee schedule change updating the definition of Trading Platform
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BYX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Its Fee Schedule To Update the Definition of Trading Platform Federal Register · Oct 26, 2026 The SEC published a notice of a rule change filed by Cboe BYX Exchange to amend the definition of "Trading Platform" in its fee schedule. The change adds a use-based category covering any system or platform through which orders of others are systematically executed electronically, with examples including broker crossing systems not filed as ATSs, systematic internalization systems, and decentralized blockchain-based or tokenized environments. The Commission also waived the 30-day operative delay.

entry.title: Comptroller of the Currency seeks comment on a new information collection for applications to issue payment stablecoins under the GENIUS Act
entry.summary: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Information Collection; Submission for OMB Review; Applications for Licensing or Registration To Issue Payment Stablecoins Under the GENIUS Act Federal Register · Oct 23, 2026 · Crypto The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gives notice of a new information collection for entities seeking to issue payment stablecoins in the United States under the GENIUS Act. The collection has been sent to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review, and the public may submit comments within the stated period. The notice also lists the factors the OCC will use to evaluate applications, including the applicant's financial condition, officers' compliance records, and redemption and risk management policies.

entry.title: SEC Review of OCC Rule Change on Allocating Clearing Fund Deposits Among Clearing Members
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; The Options Clearing Corporation; Order Setting Aside Action by Delegated Authority and Approving Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, by The Options Clearing Corporation Concerning Methodology To Allocate Clearing Fund Deposit Requirements Among Its Clearing Members To Better Align the Allocation With the Sizing of the Clearing Fund so Stress Based Risk is Fairly Allotted to Market Participants That Expose OCC to Such Stress Risk Federal Register · Oct 6, 2026 The Options Clearing Corporation proposed changing how its clearing members' Clearing Fund deposit requirements are allocated so the allocation better matches the Clearing Fund's size and stress-based risk falls fairly on participants who expose OCC to it. The SEC first approved the change under delegated authority, then Fidelity petitioned for review, and the Commission conducted a de novo review of the proposal. The Commission is assessing whether the proposal is consistent with the Exchange Act.

entry.title: Texas Stock Exchange proposed rule change on ETP listing fees and lead market maker stipends
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Adopt Listing Fees for Exchange Traded Products and Performance Standards and Daily Stipends Paid by the Exchange for Its Lead Market Maker Program Federal Register · Oct 1, 2026 The Texas Stock Exchange filed with the SEC a proposed rule change to adopt three tiers of listing fees for exchange-traded products and three tiers of minimum performance standards for lead market makers. Market makers that meet the standards would receive daily stipends paid by the exchange. The filing states the aim is to fund liquidity for newer, costlier-to-trade ETP categories.

entry.title: Cboe BZX Exchange proposes rule changes creating listing standards for options on multi-crypto-asset trusts and allowing options on ETFs
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 19.3 and Rule 19.4 To Establish Generic Listing Criteria and Continued Listing Standards for Options on Commodity-Based Trusts Holding Multiple Crypto Assets and To Permit the Listing of Options on Exchange-Traded Funds Federal Register · Oct 16, 2026 · Crypto Cboe BZX Exchange filed with the SEC a proposal to amend Rules 19.3 and 19.4 to set generic listing and continued listing standards for options on shares of commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets. The proposal also permits options on exchange-traded funds as defined under Rule 6c-11 of the Investment Company Act. It was filed as non-controversial and became effective upon publication, with comments due by November 6, 2026.

entry.title: EPA proposal to reconsider air pollution standards for gasoline distribution facilities and bulk gasoline terminals
entry.summary: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Gasoline Distribution Facilities and Standards of Performance for Bulk Gasoline Terminals Reconsideration Federal Register · Sep 28, 2026 The EPA proposes to reconsider parts of its 2024 final rule on hazardous air pollutant and performance standards for gasoline facilities. Topics include operating limits and continuous compliance for emission control devices, vapor tightness for gasoline cargo tanks, and modification criteria in the NSPS. The agency states the changes do not affect the stringency of the standards and are not expected to change VOC or HAP emissions. Public comments and a possible virtual hearing are provided for.

entry.title: Proposed rule implementing the Federal Reserve Board's responsibilities under the GENIUS Act
entry.summary: Implementing the Federal Reserve Board's Responsibilities Under the GENIUS Act Federal Register · Sep 29, 2026 · Crypto The Federal Reserve Board proposes regulations implementing the GENIUS Act for Board-supervised permitted payment stablecoin issuers and certain other entities under its jurisdiction. It also proposes rules implementing the tying prohibition in section 4(a)(8), which applies to all permitted payment stablecoin issuers. Comments are due by November 30, 2026.

entry.title: Federal Reserve proposal setting application procedures for supervised banks seeking approval for a subsidiary to issue payment stablecoins
entry.summary: Application Procedures for Board-Supervised Insured Depository Institutions Seeking Approval for a Subsidiary To Issue Payment Stablecoins Federal Register · Sep 29, 2026 · Crypto The Federal Reserve Board proposes rules under the GENIUS Act setting out how insured State member banks apply for Board approval for a subsidiary to issue payment stablecoins. The proposal would be added as subpart D of Regulation UU and would let the Board evaluate applications against statutory safety and soundness factors while limiting unnecessary burden on applicants. Comments are due by November 30, 2026.

entry.title: Interim rule setting forms and procedures for the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee to review state certifications
entry.summary: Forms and Procedures for Review of State Certifications by the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee Federal Register · Sep 30, 2026 · Crypto The Treasury Department, on behalf of the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee, issued an interim final rule establishing procedures and forms for reviewing certifications submitted by state payment stablecoin regulators under section 4(c) of the GENIUS Act. The rule takes effect September 30, 2026, but certifications will not be accepted until the information collection receives Paperwork Reduction Act approval, with Treasury to announce that date. Comments are due by November 30, 2026.

entry.title: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations general licenses 52 through 58
entry.summary: Publication of Venezuela Sanctions Regulations Web General Licenses 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, and 58 Federal Register · Sep 30, 2026 The Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control publishes in the Federal Register general licenses 52 through 58 issued under the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR part 591), which were previously posted on OFAC's website. The notice also publishes General License 5W, issued May 4, 2026, which replaces General License 5V. It sets out the transactions each license authorizes and the conditions attached to them.

entry.title: Rule on Impersonation of Government and Businesses (Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking)
entry.summary: Rule on Impersonation of Government and Businesses Federal Register · Oct 1, 2026 The Federal Trade Commission proposes starting a rulemaking to stop search engines, social media and other digital marketplace platforms from furthering government and business impersonation scams through ad optimization. The Commission is seeking public comment on whether such a rule is needed. Comments are due November 30, 2026.

entry.title: Final rule to enhance transparency and public accountability of supervisory stress test models and scenarios
entry.summary: Enhanced Transparency and Public Accountability of the Supervisory Stress Test Models and Scenarios; Modifications to the Capital Planning and Stress Capital Buffer Requirement Rule, Enhanced Prudential Standards Rule, and Regulation LL Federal Register · Oct 2, 2026 The Federal Reserve Board issued a final rule amending Regulations Y, LL, and YY to make its stress testing framework more transparent and publicly accountable. It also amends the scenario design and stress testing policy statements, finalizes the models for the 2027 stress test, and seeks public input on further model changes. Changes to FR Y-14A/Q/M stress test data collection are also finalized. The rule takes effect November 2, 2026.

entry.title: Federal scholarship tax credit (temporary rules)
entry.summary: Federal Scholarship Tax Credit Federal Register · Oct 2, 2026 The IRS issued temporary regulations implementing a new nonrefundable federal income tax credit under section 25F of the Internal Revenue Code for individuals who make qualified contributions to scholarship granting organizations (SGOs) that fund elementary and secondary education scholarships. The rules set out requirements and procedures for states electing to participate and for SGOs certified by participating states. They accompany a concurrently published notice of proposed rulemaking.

entry.title: Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (Proposed Rules)
entry.summary: Federal Scholarship Tax Credit Federal Register · Oct 2, 2026 The IRS and Treasury propose regulations for the nonrefundable federal tax credit under Internal Revenue Code section 25F. The credit applies to cash contributions to certified scholarship granting organizations that fund qualified elementary and secondary school scholarships. The document also sets the deadline for public comments and announces a public hearing.

entry.title: Proposal to prohibit certain fund transfers involving A7 Network sub-agents.
entry.summary: Proposal of Special Measure Prohibiting the Transmittal of Funds Regarding Transactions Involving the A7 Network's Sub-Agents Federal Register · Oct 5, 2026 FinCEN proposes a special measure finding that transactions with any non-U.S. company controlled by the A7 Network are a class of primary money laundering concern tied to Russian illicit finance. It proposes prohibiting covered financial institutions from certain fund transmittals involving these transactions. Written comments are due November 4, 2026.

entry.title: Withdrawal of proposed special measure targeting international crypto asset mixing
entry.summary: Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Convertible Virtual Currency Mixing, as a Class of Transactions of Primary Money Laundering Concern; Withdrawal Federal Register · Oct 6, 2026 · Crypto FinCEN withdrew its 2023 proposed rule and related finding that international convertible virtual currency (CVC) mixing is a class of transactions of primary money laundering concern under section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act. The proposal would have required enhanced recordkeeping and reporting by covered financial institutions. FinCEN cited concerns that the broad definition of CVC mixing could chill legitimate activity and impose heavy reporting burdens, and said it will continue monitoring mixer activity.

entry.title: Withdrawal of proposed rule on transactions involving convertible virtual currency or digital assets
entry.summary: Requirements for Certain Transactions Involving Convertible Virtual Currency or Digital Assets; Withdrawal Federal Register · Oct 6, 2026 · Crypto FinCEN is withdrawing a December 2020 proposed rule that would have required banks and money service businesses to report, keep records, and verify customer identity for certain convertible virtual currency transactions involving unhosted or covered wallets. It is also withdrawing an October 2023 proposal on international CVC mixing. FinCEN says it will continue to monitor CVC mixer activity.

entry.title: IEX Notice on Rule Change Setting Listing and Withdrawal Standards for Crypto Asset Trust Options and Amending IBIT Options Limits
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Investors Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Establish Listing Standards and Withdrawal Criteria for Options on Commodity-Based Trusts Holding a Single Crypto Asset or Multiple Crypto Assets and To Amend Rules Regarding Position and Exercise Limits for Options on iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF Federal Register · Oct 7, 2026 · Crypto The SEC published a notice of a proposed rule change filed by Investors Exchange LLC (IEX). The proposal would establish listing and withdrawal criteria for options on commodity-based trusts holding one or more crypto assets, and amend position and exercise limits for options on the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF. It was filed ahead of the launch of IEX Options and designated as non-controversial.

entry.title: Treasury seeks comment on extending the Digital Assets Criteria Form for threat-information sharing
entry.summary: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Information-Sharing Initiative: Digital Assets Criteria Form Federal Register · Oct 9, 2026 · Crypto The U.S. Treasury Department has published a notice requesting public comment on extending, without change, an information collection for its Information-Sharing Initiative: Digital Assets Criteria Form. The form verifies whether applicants are eligible to receive Treasury's non-public cyber threat information, collecting details such as identity, legal status, digital asset function, and cybersecurity maturity. Comments are due by December 8, 2026.

entry.title: Advance notice seeking comment on rules for crypto asset transactions and markets
entry.summary: Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets Federal Register · Oct 13, 2026 · Crypto The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on developing rules under section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act for crypto asset transactions and markets. Public comments are due by December 14, 2026. The document defines a crypto asset and notes that certain payment stablecoins may not meet the Act's definition of commodity.

entry.title: Cboe proposal to list binary options on issuers' key performance indicators, approved with Amendment No. 1
entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe Exchange, Inc.; Notice of Filing of Amendment No. 1 and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To Permit the Listing of Binary Options Overlying Key Performance Indicators Reported by Certain Issuers of Stock Federal Register · Oct 16, 2026 The SEC approved, on an accelerated basis, a Cboe Exchange rule change allowing listing of binary options on key performance indicators reported by certain stock issuers. Binary KPI options are cash-settled and pay a fixed amount if the KPI reported in an earnings-related SEC filing meets or exceeds the strike level. The notice publishes Amendment No. 1 for comment.

entry.title: Further Definition of “Swap” to Exclude Casino-Style Gambling Products (CFTC interim final rule)
entry.summary: Further Definition of “Swap” To Exclude Casino-Style Gambling Products Federal Register · Oct 19, 2026 The Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an interim final rule codifying its longstanding position that casino-style gambling products, including sportsbook wagers and casino games, are excluded from the definition of “swap.” The rule takes effect October 19, 2026, and comments are due by November 18, 2026.

entry.title: Further Definition of “Swap” – Inclusions (CFTC proposed rule to explicitly cover event contracts)
entry.summary: Further Definition of “Swap”-Inclusions Federal Register · Oct 19, 2026 The Commodity Futures Trading Commission proposes to further define the term “swap” so that it explicitly includes event contracts, including those based on sports, political, cultural, and weather-related events. The proposal was published in the Federal Register on October 19, 2026, with comments due November 18, 2026.

entry.title: State Justice Institute FY 2027 grant guideline notice
entry.summary: Grant Guideline; Notice Federal Register · Oct 21, 2026 This Federal Register notice sets out the FY 2027 grant guideline of the State Justice Institute (SJI), covering its administrative, programmatic and financial requirements. It describes eligible recipients, quarterly application deadlines, and the Priority Investment Areas, which include opioids and behavioral health responses and access to justice and procedural fairness.

entry.title: Proposed rule on notifying members of share insurance coverage
entry.summary: Notification to Members/Shareholders Federal Register · Oct 21, 2026 The NCUA proposes amending 12 CFR 745.13 to remove the requirement that FICUs provide hard copies of prescribed share insurance materials. Credit unions would choose the notification method, such as linking to NCUA or eCFR online resources. NCUA plans to discontinue its "Your Insured Funds" brochure and update its share insurance website. Comments are due December 21, 2026.

entry.title: SNAP EBT card security measures (proposed rule to modernize benefit cards)
entry.summary: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Electronic Benefits Transfer Card Security Measures Federal Register · Oct 23, 2026 The USDA's Food and Nutrition Administration proposes changes to SNAP regulations to modernize Electronic Benefit Transfer cards and align them with consumer payment industry standards. The document says current magnetic-stripe cards secured only by PINs are vulnerable to skimming and cloning, putting benefits at risk. Written comments are due by December 22, 2026.

entry.title: Publicis and LiveRamp: Analysis of Proposed Consent Order Seeking Public Comment
entry.summary: Publicis and LiveRamp; Analysis of Proposed Agreement Containing Consent Order To Aid Public Comment Federal Register · Oct 23, 2026 The Federal Trade Commission has published a proposed consent agreement and analysis concerning Publicis's planned acquisition of LiveRamp and is seeking public comment. The FTC alleges the deal could substantially lessen competition in U.S. media agency services and audience data services markets. The proposed order would require, for five years, non-discriminatory supply of LiveRamp's data connectivity services and protection of competitors' sensitive information.

entry.title: OCC notice seeking comment on new reporting forms for permitted payment stablecoin issuers
entry.summary: Agency Information Collection Activities: Proposed Information Collection; Submission for OMB Review; Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency Federal Register · Oct 23, 2026 · Crypto The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency published a notice of a new information collection covering weekly (Form PS-01) and quarterly (Form PS-02) reporting forms and instructions for permitted payment stablecoin issuers. The forms support compliance with the GENIUS Act and the OCC's final implementing rule. Public comments are due by November 23, 2026.

entry.title: OCC final rule implementing the GENIUS Act for stablecoin issuance by OCC-supervised entities
entry.summary: Implementing the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act for the Issuance of Stablecoins by Entities Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency Federal Register · Oct 23, 2026 · Crypto The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issues a final rule implementing the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoin issuance and related activities by entities under its jurisdiction, effective January 18, 2027. The document responds to about 328 public comments on the March 2026 proposal, covering reserve asset management, redemption, capital requirements and the yield prohibition. It also explains that BSA/AML requirements will be addressed in a separate rulemaking.

entry.title: Treasury notice seeking comment on information return forms and related collection
entry.summary: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; U.S. Information Returns and Related Forms, Schedules, Attachments, and Published Guidance Federal Register · Oct 23, 2026 The U.S. Treasury Department submits an information collection covering 51 information return forms, schedules and published guidance to the Office of Management and Budget for review, and invites public comment. The notice explains that the burden for these forms will be estimated using the RAAS Taxpayer Burden Model rather than the prior form-by-form method, and that all forms will be grouped under OMB Control Number 1545-0108.

entry.title: Outbound Investment Security Program Regulations: Treasury's proposed rule implementing restrictions on U.S. investments in sensitive foreign technologies
entry.summary: Outbound Investment Security Program Regulations Federal Register · Oct 26, 2026 The Treasury Department's Office of Investment Security proposes regulations to implement Subtitle C of the COINS Act, codified at Title VIII of the Defense Production Act. The rule would require U.S. persons to notify Treasury of certain transactions involving foreign persons engaged in notifiable technologies, and prohibit certain other transactions involving foreign persons engaged in prohibited technologies. It incorporates existing program definitions where consistent with the statute and adds applicability dates. Written comments are due by December 7, 2026.
